description: Eerste Helmersstraat 116-122 (1893): 6 m red-brown brick fronts of a ground and two upper storeys under a white moulded cornice at 10.8 m; three axes of two-light windows under a top light, each dressed in white stone: three blocks bonded into each jamb, a keystone over the flat head, a sill; an iron balconette on the centre axis of the top storey; a white pedimented dormer

pediment-dormer.note: 116-122: one white timber dormer with a pediment (120: carved, with box dormers beside it), centred

door-right.note: 116, 118: double house door under a fanlight on the right axis

rhythm.identicalBays: every storey: 3 windows under a top light, one width
rhythm.symmetry: upper storeys symmetric; door right (or left, mirrored)
rhythm.roofline: white moulded cornice at 10.8 m; one pedimented dormer

match.note: Eerste Helmersstraat 116-122 (1893), 6 m; cornice 10.8 m on the strip; the skyline reads the dormer tops at 13.2-13.8 m (frontSkylineM)

evidence.citation: strip.jpg 2024-11-29 (and the 2023-01-12 strip at a 2.4 m camera height that placement now uses) pands 10-11 (118, 116) at 1.8x with a metre grid: ground windows 0.5-3.3 m, storey-1 windows 4.4-6.6 (top light 6.0-6.6), storey-2 7.6-9.7; keystones 0.3 m over each head; three jamb blocks a side 0.12 m high reaching 0.14 m at 0.17, 0.48 and 0.81 of the window; balconette 7.2-7.9 m on the centre axis; cornice 10.2-10.9 m

schemaLimits: the window sills under the keystone surround are the library's keystone dressing only (the photo has white sills too)
the dormer is the library pediment dormer; 120 has a carved dormer flanked by two box dormers
notes: Palette: strip medians of 116 (shaded) and 118 (sunlit), 2024-11-29; placed pands take their own measured wall.
